conversation.user: I just dropped this skill kit into my project — can you set it up so the AI is ready to work?

conversation.ai: Sure — starting initialize. Do you want a light scan (skeleton first) or a full scan (fill in all the detail)?

Scanned the repo: it's a NestJS monorepo with two apps — live-service and live-consumer — on Postgres. Inbound: I found each app's routes/controllers; Outbound: I found the gateway/client calls in the code. Quick check — is the domain a live-selling system?

Done — created context/gateway-directory.md from the format. Inbound is split into one table per app (live-service, live-consumer); Outbound is grouped by target system as found in the code. Anything the scan couldn't fully resolve is left for self-learn to fill during real workflow runs.

evals.expected_output: AI enters initialize, asks light/full, reports what it scanned + asks to confirm the uncertain parts, then writes context/gateway-directory.md following gateway-directory-format.md
expectations: AI enters the initialize skill (doesn't just do it ad-hoc)
asks light vs full scan before starting (Phase 1)
reports what it scanned itself (NestJS 2 apps, postgres, inbound routes, outbound gateway calls) — doesn't make the user provide everything
for anything the scan can't resolve → asks back (e.g. confirm domain) or leaves it for self-learn — does not guess, does not mock
writes to context/gateway-directory.md per the Target in the format (not elsewhere)
copies the template's format into the target (## How to use + per-section templates + ## References + ## Role & Boundary) but not the Target line / ## How to scan
## Inbound Gateway has one table per app: ### live-service and ### live-consumer
## Outbound Gateway groups by target system (one ### per system), not by gateway-class/function name
every table uses columns: endpoint | condition | purpose | bridge | function | note
bridge is an id in the form <service>(<path>), not a function name
function holds where the code lives (controller/handler for inbound, gateway/client for outbound); request/response shapes are NOT written here (they live in gateway-contract.md)
an endpoint with multiple variants is split into one row per variant via the condition key (e.g. action=RESERVE vs action=RELEASE)
Phase 2: checks for existing docs to migrate — none here, so nothing is migrated
